findings.description: New skill omits `disable-model-invocation: true`, so it is model-invoked and its description loads every turn. The README row lists it as 'Auto or /ci-and-agent-config' but nothing states why natural phrasing must trigger it. writing-for-agents/SKILL.md 'House rules' (line 90) says: 'Default new skills to user-invoked (`disable-model-invocation: true`). Keep model-invocation only when natural task phrasing must trigger the skill, or another skill calls it.' Either add the flag, or add a line to the skill or README giving the reason.

The diagram annotation `(red first)` only restates `red → green → refactor` in the same line and says nothing new. Drop the parenthetical, or name the companion plugin's `tdd` skill there as the other two edits in this PR do.

The headline reads "7 skills, 12 subagents, 7 deterministic hooks". The PR edits that line to fix the skill count, but the component table below it, `.claude/README.md` and the `agents/README.md` catalog (the last not opened) give 13 agents and 10 hooks. The 12 and 7 were stale before this PR.

process_issues.description: Gated out correctness, security, maintainability, context and spec: the diff is markdown prose only (skill deletions, skill/README/doc rewrites), with no executable logic, trust boundary, infra surface, or spec source (no closing issues).

The reviewer briefs gave the restored config path as `.claude-pr/<path relative to .claude>`. The PR's copies actually sit at `.claude-pr/.claude/...`, so the conventions reviewer's first reads missed until it found the right path.
